params.content: Delia, I did take rest—more than enough, if you count the hours I spent worrying in place of sleep. Thank you for asking, and for being patient about the wages; I have paid what was owed. There was a story my old mentor told me about a medicine that could cure anything, and I have spent half my life learning where that story ends. I will not ask you to promise what no pharmacist can promise. Let us keep the shelves honest, and speak plainly when a case is beyond us.
params.intent: answer Delia honestly and affirm our pharmacy work

params.content: Not long enough for the worry to deserve the dignity of a proper illness, Delia—only long enough to make a man count imagined costs on his fingers. I am glad you asked. You kept the pharmacy steady while I was making a story out of every possible failure; thank you. And now, youngster, I should hear the town before I presume it wants another long tale from me.
params.intent: answer Delia warmly and thank her for her care

params.content: A few nights, Delia—not so many that I can put a number on them without pretending certainty. When I first took up the trade, there was an illness the town's medicines could not touch, and I learned that worry may keep watch long after the patient is gone. But I am still here, and I will try to sleep more honestly than I have been worrying. Thank you, youngster.
params.intent: answer Delia about the old grief without claiming certainty
